request.recipient: 2026 Treasury Reserve Smart Contract stake address stake1784sdxt6jjennmstphgdu7l7c2scf5d02a6cve2dgn5s2kq5u3j9v, with later transfer to a project-specific smart contract for the vendor when contract and readiness conditions are met.
request.what: Treasury withdrawal to fund Mithril Protocol continuous development through Intersect on behalf of the vendor.

claims.claim: Mithril is presented as solving the cost and complexity of securely accessing and verifying Cardano blockchain state through stake-based threshold multi-signatures.
The proposal states Mithril enables rapid trustless verification of Cardano state without relying on the entire chain.
The proposal claims faster sync times lower onboarding friction and support tooling for exchanges, wallets, monitoring, bridges, light wallets, full wallets, and light clients.
The proposal states it achieved the required 67% support threshold in the 2026 Intersect Budget Process Hydra Voting phase.
The proposal claims the requested withdrawal does not breach the applicable 350M Net Change Limit for Epoch 613 to Epoch 713 at the time of submission.
The budget allocates 3,699,440 ada to Mithril Protocol Continuous Development and 110,983 ada to the Intersect Budget Administration fee.
The proposal states audit, oversight, reporting obligations, and milestone-based disbursement controls are included through Intersect and technically capable third parties.
The proposal states Teragone has not previously received direct funding from Cardano treasury or community governance programs, while prior Mithril work was funded by IOG.
Intersect says it will use Sundae Labs treasury management smart contracts, with named TRSC and PSSC addresses, admin and leadership sign-off requirements, and an external Oversight Committee.
The proposal states the community can audit and track the withdrawn ada through a public dashboard and on-chain verification.

summary: The proposal requests 3,810,423 ada for Mithril Protocol continuous development and Intersect administration, with cited budget-process references, smart-contract custody arrangements, oversight roles, and NCL compliance claims, but limited anchor-level detail on milestones, schedule, or concrete deliverable acceptance criteria.
